- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 5–7 days of a new 30d forecast window; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias for early days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.0–0.4), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is >10% above 14d moving average, reduce by 1–3% to align with historical reversion pattern.
